$comment: Illustrative machine-readable CBOM profile for procurement. DERIVED: extends the interface disclosure baseline v0.8 (draft) and adds no per-interface attribute. It selects and tightens, which places it in the disclosure group (draft decision 0023): a document rich enough for the baseline, and with the implementing library stated, answers it without being reissued. DRAFT: sits in drafts/procurement/ until the baseline v0.8 is promoted with decision 0022.
title: Procurement and Tender Conformance (Example)

objective.$comment: C1. The consumer is the buyer, not the operator the product will later serve. The decision is about the tender response, and every rule below traces to a reason a buyer would send a response back.
objective.consumer: A buyer evaluating tender responses for a product it will operate but did not build and cannot inspect.
objective.decision: Whether a supplier's cryptographic disclosure is complete and specific enough to compare with other responses and to hold the supplier to over the contract, or whether it must be clarified or rejected.
decisionOptions: accept the disclosure for evaluation alongside other responses
return it for clarification, naming the failing rules
reject the response as non-compliant with the tender's disclosure requirement

scope.$comment: C11. Narrows the base's accepted lifecycle stages by removing 'intended'. A tender response describes the product being offered; a statement of what it is meant to do is a promise, and belongs in the commercial response where its status is understood.

overrides.note: Tightened by removing withholdability, as the migration profile does. A buyer holds the product for the life of the contract and must be able to match every interface to library advisories during it. A tender response is made under the tender's confidentiality terms, which is where a supplier's reason to withhold the library is answered.

productRules.description: Product declares at least one storage interface for key material at rest, or states why it has none
productRules.note: The structural rule a buyer most needs after P2. Responses describe the interfaces traffic crosses and are silent about where keys are kept. A product that keeps no keys, or keeps them in a hardware module outside the product, satisfies the rule by saying so, the same way P2 treats a product with no management surface.

productRules.description: Product states coverage of all interfaces, or of all externally reachable ones
productRules.note: P4 requires coverage to be stated. A partial disclosure cannot be compared across responses, because a missing interface could be absent or merely unlisted, so a buyer returns it. Stated as a new rule on the same attribute rather than as an override of P4, with its own narrower vocabulary.

exclusions.item: Scoring, ranking or weighting of responses
exclusions.reason: A judgement, and the buyer's own. The profile decides whether a disclosure can be evaluated, not how it scores. See decision 0002.
Asked for by a change-planning profile. A buyer who needs them names the PQC migration profile in the tender as well, and the supplier answers both with one richer document.

exclusions.item: Algorithm requirements such as a minimum key size or an approved list
exclusions.reason: Policy applied to the disclosed facts, not a fact about the disclosure. A buyer evaluates them with its own versioned policy over a conforming document.

artifacts.$comment: C9. The examples are the Keycloak pass document from the PQC migration drafts, unchanged, and a copy with the storage interface removed. Verdicts depend on the same evaluator gaps as the migration examples (K7 services, K9 inheritance); see README.md.

changelog.summary: Initial draft. Extends the interface disclosure baseline v0.8: narrows accepted lifecycle stages, tightens I9 by removing withholdability, and adds product rules P5 (storage interface or stated absence) and P6 (coverage at least all-external).
